chapters.body: At a Pesta Sukan softball tournament in Penang, May Yim played for Perak and Colin Schooling played for Singapore's Pirates team. He had been a sportsman at Raffles Institution, running hurdles and playing water polo before national softball. She had grown up poor in Ipoh, getting new clothes only at Chinese New Year, and had become a chartered accountant while he worked as a businessman. They married in 1983. After several miscarriages, their only child arrived twelve years later, on 16 June 1995 in Singapore, when May was 40. "He was a miracle - and an amazingly easy baby!"

quote.text: He was a miracle - and an amazingly easy baby!

chapters.title: Twelve Years Waiting
chapters.turn: The water would test that luck before long.
chapters.voice: Twelve years of miscarriages ended with one easy baby.

chapters.body: At three he started lessons with Vincent Poon at Tanah Merah Country Club. His mother could swim no more than a doggy paddle, and her son was a fearless water baby, so she had insisted he learn to be water-safe. Over four years Poon pitted him against older, bigger boys. Once he refused to race a much taller boy in a 50 m butterfly. Poon told him size mattered less than being fearless, and he won. He worked hard and listened through those early races. He told SwimSwam in 2025 about that start: "I didn't start swimming to win the Olympics. It was just to be safe in the water."

quote.text: I didn't start swimming to win the Olympics. It was just to be safe in the water.

chapters.title: A Mother Who Could Not Swim
chapters.turn: Soon someone else would show him how far water could take him.
chapters.voice: Fearlessness mattered more than size in that small pool.

chapters.body: On holidays in Ipoh he was in the pool by 5am, at the city council pool or the family pool. At home in Singapore, Filipina helper Yolanda 'Auntie Yolly' Pascual had joined the household in 1997; he called her a second mum and still asked her for massages. His father took him to golf, to bowling trips in Kuala Lumpur and to eat at the Lagoon hawker centre at East Coast Park. After meeting his grand-uncle Lloyd Valberg, Singapore's first Olympian at London 1948, his Olympic obsession began. His mother played every sport with him, and friends saw a boy who could not stand losing. "He'll always say 'I want to be No. 1'."

quote.text: He'll always say 'I want to be No. 1'.

chapters.title: Auntie Yolly and 5am Pool
chapters.turn: Then a bespectacled teenager met his hero.
chapters.voice: Holidays never paused the swimming, even at dawn.

chapters.body: Monkeys were stealing energy bars from the pool deck at the Singapore Island Country Club. It was 2008, and the United States team was training in Singapore before Beijing. Michael Phelps was there. Joseph was 13 and bespectacled, and he asked Phelps for a photo. He wanted to be like him. The two later recalled that week and chasing the monkeys that stole the bars. He remembered it. He put his debt simply: "I wanted to be like him as a kid. So a lot of this is because of Michael."

quote.text: I wanted to be like him as a kid. So a lot of this is because of Michael.

chapters.title: The Monkeys and the Photo
chapters.turn: He would soon ask for something much bigger.
chapters.voice: A photo with Phelps gave the boy a fixed point.

chapters.body: At 14 he pleaded to go to the Bolles School in Florida; his mother first said no. He later admitted he was hard to coach at first and had not wanted to be there. The first year apart was the hardest: he was homesick and not used to independence. Colin's one request to coach Sergio Lopez was about character, not times. His parents took turns living with him in the United States for months at a time, averaging about three weeks a year together as three. The family spent about US$1 million (S$1.35 million) on training and education, mortgaging their home, selling a house in Perth and cashing an endowment plan. May still wore Marks & Spencer trousers she had bought in her working days in 1990. "I cried all the time. He did too."

quote.text: I cried all the time. He did too.

chapters.title: Mum, Let Me Go
chapters.turn: A first major meet would test that investment.
chapters.voice: Three weeks a year together bought a future.

chapters.body: Minutes before his 200 m butterfly heat at London 2012, officials rejected his cap and goggles. Aged 17, he found replacements in a hurry in London, then swam 1:59.18 and finished 26th of 37. At home his father, a handyman, had built swimming contraptions for his son and kept thick folders of statistics and research through those years. Afterwards an online comment stayed with him for a long time, that Singapore will never have an Olympic champion. He said afterwards: "I'm only 17 and I have a long way to go."

quote.text: I'm only 17 and I have a long way to go.

chapters.title: The Wrong Cap
chapters.turn: Stronger company would soon surround him.
chapters.voice: A faulty cap could not end the longer plan.

chapters.body: In Kazan he touched third in the 100 m butterfly at the World Championships in 2015. In 2014 he had taken up a place at the University of Texas, training under Eddie Reese. The move kept him under Reese through the next summers and toward the bronze. The bronze confirmed the progress. After Rio, Phelps pointed back to that season as the start of the run. Phelps told ESPN in August 2016: "Joe's tough. Obviously he's had a great year last year" He kept working under Reese into the next season.

quote.text: Joe's tough. Obviously he's had a great year last year

chapters.title: Bronze in Kazan
chapters.turn: Rio was only a year away.
chapters.voice: Kazan bronze showed the Texas work was paying off.

chapters.body: On 12 August 2016 in Rio he won the 100 m butterfly in an Olympic record 50.39. Phelps, Chad le Clos and Laszlo Cseh tied for silver behind him. In the stands May did not even notice the three-way tie for second. Colin, unwell, had stayed in Singapore and watched at the home of Joseph's friend Teo Zhen Ren. On the victory lap Joseph told Phelps it was crazy, and Phelps patted his back and said he knew. Colin's first words to his son afterwards carried everything: "I love you. Son, you have done the nation very proud."

quote.text: I love you. Son, you have done the nation very proud.

chapters.title: Fifty Point Three Nine
chapters.turn: Dawn would feel strangely quiet after that noise.
chapters.voice: Fifty point three nine, and three silvers behind him.

chapters.body: At dawn the next morning he had breakfast alone with headphones on, watching the sunrise from the dining hall. He had described his career so far as breaking through a wall, taking the blow as the first man through. Then came the flight home, an open-top bus parade through crowds on 18 August 2016 and S$1 million under the national award scheme. From August to December fame overwhelmed him, and he did not get back in the pool until December, which made Eddie Reese nervous. That autumn he tore his bicep twice and later said he should have sat out the season. He knew one thing at sunrise: "My life will never be the same again."

quote.text: My life will never be the same again.

chapters.title: Breakfast at Sunrise
chapters.turn: The honours hid a body starting to break.
chapters.voice: Sunrise, headphones on, alone before the noise returned.

chapters.body: On 7 August 2017 an orchid hybrid, Dendrobium Joseph Schooling, was named after him. After the 2017 worlds he put on about 7 kg and faced public abuse about his weight. He graduated in economics in December 2018 and finished 24th in the 100 m butterfly at the 2019 worlds. Phelps asked him whether he swam for the people in the stands or for himself. He could not answer at first. In February 2020 he moved to Christiansburg, Virginia, to train with Sergio Lopez again, recognised there only once, at a Chipotle. "Look, everything crashed in 2019."
chapters.title: Why Do You Swim?
chapters.voice: An orchid bloomed while results wilted.

chapters.body: At the Tokyo Olympics, held in 2021, he went out in the heats of the 100 m butterfly. On 18 November 2021 Colin died of cancer, aged 73. Joseph posted a childhood photo of the two of them with only a heart. May said her own farewell. In August 2022 he admitted using cannabis overseas in May while on leave for the SEA Games and apologised, saying he had been through a very tough period. He called it weakness. "It is hard to say goodbye, so let's begin with 'see you again'."

quote.text: It is hard to say goodbye, so let's begin with 'see you again'.

chapters.title: See You Again
chapters.turn: What came next began where he started.
chapters.voice: He captioned his father with a single heart.

chapters.body: On 2 April 2024, at 28, he announced his retirement and spoke to reporters at the Chinese Swimming Club. He remembered being four, hopping into the unreasonably freezing pool. His mother noted in an open letter that he had moved into his late father's office. He worked in venture capital, played golf and ran his own swim school that taught water safety. The reason for teaching was the reason he had started. He then explained the ending plainly: "I woke up not feeling the same excitement to go to practice."

quote.text: I woke up not feeling the same excitement to go to practice.

chapters.title: Dad's Office
chapters.turn: Water-safe from the start, to the end.
chapters.voice: He moved into his late father's office.

conflicts.choice: About US$1 million (S$1.35 million) with mortgaged home, Perth sale and endowment cashed.
2008 meeting at Singapore Island Country Club; first lessons at Tanah Merah Country Club.
Says overseas in May, not Vietnam.
Uses blog reprints but keeps bylines and dates.
